How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | > **Note** – The API expects the *interfaceType* value in **lower‑case** (`ethernet`). > The *infoType* value is also case‑sensitive (`Speed`). --- ## 1. Full URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` --- ## 2. Example `curl` command ```bash curl -k \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -u admin:admin123 \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` * `-k` – skip certificate verification (use only in test environments). * Replace `admin:admin123` with your actual ND credentials. * The response will be a JSON payload containing the requested speed data. --- ## 3. Example Python `requests` snippet ```python import requests url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" params = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } # Basic auth – replace with your credentials auth = ("admin", "admin123") # Disable SSL verification only for testing response = requests.get(url, params=params, auth=auth, verify=False) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` --- ## 4. Using the provided tool (`functions.requests_get`) If you want to let the assistant actually perform the GET request (within the sandbox), you can invoke the tool like this: ```json { "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", "params": { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } } ``` > **Caution** – The tool will attempt to reach the specified IP. If the IP is not reachable from the sandbox, the call will fail. Use it only when you have network connectivity to the ND instance. --- ## 5. Quick checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✅ | Base URL (`https:///sedgeapi/v1/...`) | | ✅ | Correct endpoint (`/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo`) | | ✅ | Query parameters in the right order & case | | ✅ | Authentication header or Basic Auth | | ✅ | Accept/Content‑Type headers set to `application/json` | | ✅ | SSL verification handled appropriately | That’s all you need to generate and send a RESTful API request to fetch the *Speed* information for the specified interface on Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy querying!
